items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: I was playing with the Basie band in Cincinnati years ago with Count Basie... Freddie Green turned around to me and said... I got the biggest hug from him when I left the band the last time I saw him.

ctx.x: That’s interesting because we’ll probably talk about swinging at a slow tempo in a few minutes.

It’s hard to do. It’s not as easy as you would think. It’s harder to play slow because you have to really give each beat its full value, which is a direct quote from Freddie Green. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

You know I was playing with the Basie band in Cincinnati years ago with Count Basie, and we were playing with the Cincinnati Symphony. And we were at rehearsal and we were playing something very soft and precious. And at the end of the take, you know, Freddie Green turned around to me and said, “Give each beat its full value of time.” I said, “Freddie, you never talked to me so much before.” But it was a classic statement.
